provenance.author: block B1 writer (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Beat realised in four sections: the birthday gifts in the hall (sword, shield, cloak, pies, Mali's book), Arth's straw-man present and Cai riding, Arth trying to hold the real sword (Cynyr looks at Elen), and the evening scene in which Dafi becomes Arth's friend.

Primary target G08: more than 25 possession sentences with gyda fi / ti / fe / hi / Cai, Oes … gyda ti? and Does dim … gyda fi. Contrasts with earlier forms: 'Cleddyf Cai yw e' (genitive, Pennod 2) ↔ 'Mae cleddyf gyda Cai'; 'Mae Cai'n cael cleddyf' (receives) ↔ 'Mae cleddyf gyda Cai' (has); Oes … gyda ti? reuses Pennod 6 Oes.
Secondary pattern per writer_notes: gallu / hoffi / cael + verb-noun with no mutation (Mae Cai'n gallu marchogaeth; Dw i'n hoffi marchogaeth; Rwyt ti'n cael dal cleddyf go iawn).

Plan gap: 'fe' is needed for 'gyda fe' (the target paradigm) but is not a planned lexeme. Added as a form of cy-e in lexicon-deltas/pennod-08.json (the cy-e card already says 'fe after conjugated prepositions'). Also added 'gydag' (before a vowel) to cy-gyda for 'gydag Arth'.

Threads: thr-tad-arth echo (Cynyr watches Arth holding the real sword and looks at Elen; Mali: 'Pam mae Dad yn edrych ar Mam?'); thr-beards echo (Cai: 'ble mae barf Cai?' – Cynyr: 'Dim ond pymtheg oed wyt ti!'). Myrddin's 'Rwyt ti'n fach nawr. Nawr.' echoes his 'Ydy, nawr' from Pennod 5.
Family words recycled per the pilot note (brawd, chwaer, plant, mab via Cai), and tref, pell, agos.

Applied gpt-6-astra review (2026-10-12): 'rhedeg i Arth' (calque) recast as 'Mae Dafi'n dod o'r het ac yn rhedeg yn gyflym'; Pensa A a5 now cues possession (a book that is Mali's), B b6 now needs hoffi (gallu cannot take a noun object), C c1/c2/c6 accept further correct answers; gydag rule stated as 'before a vowel sound'. 'Pam rwyt ti …?' kept (Mynediad De form). Not taken: 'taro' for the sword hitting the straw man (new word); 'mae e'n mynd i'r dyn gwellt' stays, with the scene picture carrying the impact.

Age pattern 'Dim ond pymtheg / un ar ddeg oed wyt ti / dw i' is emphatic fronting before G29: model review judges it natural; recorded here as a limited exception for age statements (integrator: add to the fronting rule's whitelist).
Checker warnings left: recall for pen-blwydd and marchog (each recurs in Pennod 9 or 10 here; the second recurrence must come from Penodau 11–13, written by other writers).

Running words about 930 against 850 (window 765–935, at the top): the chapter also carries next-five-chapter recall for Penodau 3–7 (breakfast foods, yfed, gardd, gweithio, chwarae, chwilio, galw, oer, carreg, sŵn; Pennod 7 sefyll, cymryd, bwced, gwynt, dail, adar, distaw, prysur, clust). Each recall item sits inside an event (birthday breakfast, Cai riding, the evening search for Arth).

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19 (docs/reviews/welsh-russian-lessons-2026-10-19.md): Pensa bank ambiguities fixed: b9 'does dim ___ gyda fe' fitted both arian and the bank word aur, so aur leaves the bank (12 words, still 3 spare); b7 'mae e'n ___ i Arth' also fitted anrheg, now cued by mutual liking (→ ffrind). A a10 accepts the short 'Ydw'; C c1 accepts 'Cai yw'r marchog'.

review_questions.question: [?] 'gydag Arth' before a vowel (written standard) vs 'gyda Arth' (common in speech): which should the course use? The course uses unmutated personal names after prepositions.

review_questions.question: [?] Recast from 'mae e'n rhedeg i Arth' (calque; at is not taught until Pennod 16) to 'Mae Dafi'n dod o'r het ac yn rhedeg yn gyflym. Nawr mae e ar Arth …': natural?

review_questions.question: [?] 'Dw i'n hoffi'r anrheg yn fawr' (I like the present very much): natural southern usage?

grammar.nodyn_en: Welsh says 'a sword is with Cai' for 'Cai has a sword': Mae cleddyf gyda Cai. The thing owned is usually indefinite, so questions use Oes …? and negatives Does dim …, as in Pennod 6. Gallu (can), hoffi (like) and cael (be allowed to) take a second verb-noun with no mutation.
